licenses.text:
Anonymous, Beowulf, translated by John Lesslie Hall.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/anonymous/beowulf/john-lesslie-hall

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Anonymous, the author: no death year, because the work is anonymous.
- John Lesslie Hall, the translator and writer of the introduction or preface, died 1938 (Wikidata Q6244660, P570 1938-01-01).

First publication of the text used: 1908, the English translation by John Lesslie Hall. The country of first publication is not stated in the facts. The Anglo-Saxon original was written between 975 and 1010. (SE colophon: 'Beowulf is thought to have been written between 975 and 1010. It was translated from Anglo-Saxon in 1908 by John Lesslie Hall.')

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the translation was first published in 1908, before 1931, so the text is in the United States public domain. The edition's rights statement quoted below says the same.
- Country of origin: Two layers, checked separately. Original: Anglo-Saxon work, anonymous, written between 975 and 1010. An anonymous work written before 1800 is public domain in every country. Translation (English): the possible countries are the United Kingdom, Ireland, the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, India and South Africa. Each has a term of life + 70 years or less. The translator John Lesslie Hall (died 1938) left the public domain in each of them on 1 January 2009, so the translation is public domain in each. The country of first publication therefore makes no difference.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

Sources of these facts:
- SE colophon of this edition (https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/anonymous/beowulf/john-lesslie-hall): quoted above.
- Wikidata Q6244660 (John Lesslie Hall), P570 1938-01-01.
